Smokers are over-represented in this stratum (1000 vs 500 babies).

description: Normal birth weight babies (≥2500g). Smoker infants (A): 995/1000=99.5% survival. Non-smoker infants (B): 4980/5000=99.6% survival. Non-smokers barely win (0.1pp). Non-smokers vastly outnumber smokers here (5000 vs 1000). Pooled, non-smokers (B) win because this stratum dominates B's total, and B wins it. The pooled result reverses the LBW stratum finding — a partial (type-B) paradox driven by the LBW vs NBW allocation imbalance.
name: bwp-nbw
